result.title: Quality-Governed Deep Learning Network for Brain Tumor MRI Segmentation
result.summary: The segmentation of brain tumors from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an essential step for computer-aided neuro-oncology, treatment planning and follow-up. While effective encoder-decoder representations are achieved by U-Net and Attention U-Net, the skip sections of the network can generate weak-contrast or noisy responses in the case of heterogeneous boundaries of the tumor. In this paper, we introduce a Quality-Governed Deep Learning Network (QGDL-Net) that can be used for binary tumor segmentation from FLAIR MRI slices. The proposed model is able to predict the slice quality based on contrast and SNR statistics and to fine-tune the encoder features prior to decoding by learnable quality gates. We used the 80:20 train-validation split for experiments with BraTS 2021. QGDL-Net achieved a Dice of 0.9747, IoU of 0.9506, precision of 0.9755, recall of 0.9739, F1 of 0.9747 and accuracy of 0.9982, outperforming U-Net and Attention U-Net. The EigenCAM maps and segmentation overlays provide better tumor localization and interpretable activation around the lesion regions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 QGDL-Net：先依据对比度与 SNR 统计预测 MRI 切片质量，再用可学习质量门控在解码前微调编码器特征，用于 BraTS 2021 FLAIR 的脑肿瘤二分类分割，报告 Dice 0.9747 等指标优于 U-Net 与 Attention U-Net。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以输入质量统计驱动门控来调制特征的思路，可能与 LVR 中按证据可靠性筛选视觉信息、门控状态更新的机制存在可供核查的方法线索；但论文本身只做分割精度，未涉及推理状态或 VLM 推理。
